fix(open-sse): codex api compatibility and sse translation fixes

- Codex: Extract system messages from input and merge into instructions field.
- Codex: Normalize assistant message content type from 'input_text' to 'output_text'.
- Translator: Add role 'assistant' in the first delta chunk when translating OpenAI Responses to OpenAI format.
- Translator: Skip null flush chunks in translateResponse when formats match.
- Stream: Buffer and preserve 'event:' lines in Responses API SSE translate mode.
Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/master' into fix/ollama-freetier-apikey-connection-count

fix(providers): count apikey connections for ollama freeTier provider

The /dashboard/providers/ list counts a connection only when its
authType matches the authType(s) derived for the catalog card. The
ollama entry is category:freeTier but lacks authType/authModes, so the
UI helper M() falls back to 'oauth' and filters by authType='oauth'.
The actual providerConnections row for Ollama Cloud is stored with
authType='apikey' (and the upstream registration of any new Ollama
Cloud connection is also 'apikey'). As a result the Ollama card
shows 'No connections' / no on-off toggle even when the connection is
active and testStatus=active.

This adds authType:'apikey', authModes:['apikey'] to the ollama
catalog entry, mirroring the same pattern upstream already applied to
gemini, nvidia, and openrouter in commit 1319dea6 (fix(providers):
count apikey connections for freeTier providers).

fix(codebuddy-intl): normalize messages to CodeBuddy chat shape

CodeBuddy Global (/v2/chat/completions) rejects the plain OpenAI message
shape with '11101 Parse message failed: invalid request'. It requires a
leading system prompt and user content as typed text blocks, not a bare
string. Normalize messages before sending: prepend 'You are CodeBuddy Code.',
drop upstream system/developer prompts, and wrap string user content as
[{type:text,text}].

feat(codebuddy-intl): implement usage/quota tracking

Add a usage handler for codebuddy-intl so Quota Tracker shows credit
packages instead of 'Usage API not implemented'. The intl billing endpoint
(https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/billing/meter/get-user-resource) returns the
same nested Tencent payload (data.Response.Data.Accounts[]) as CN, so the CN
handler is refactored into a shared getCodeBuddyUsage(providerId, ...) with
getCodeBuddyCnUsage/getCodeBuddyIntlUsage wrappers. Register the intl
transport.usage.url and the codebuddy-intl entry in USAGE_HANDLERS.

fix(codebuddy-cn): replace CLI agent system prompts to dodge Tencent filter

Tencent flags CLI agent system prompts ("You are Claude Code, Anthropic's
official CLI...") as prompt injection / sensitive content and rejects the
whole request. Detect agent prompts with a length catch-all (>2000 chars)
plus an identity-marker regex, and swap them for a neutral prompt while
leaving legitimate user system prompts untouched. content may arrive as a
string or as typed blocks ([{type:text,text}]) depending on the client
format, so flatten before matching and preserve the original shape on
replacement so Claude-format requests are covered too.

fix(cooldown): honour provider-reported quota reset times

An account whose quota is spent for hours or a month was put back into
rotation minutes later, failed again, and kept failing until the quota
actually returned. Three separate ceilings caused it:

- MAX_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS truncated every provider-reported reset to
  30 min. codex `resets_at` runs 5-6h out; cloudcode-pa returns
  `quotaResetTimeStamp` up to ~150h out. It is now a sanity ceiling
  (31 days) whose only job is rejecting nonsense timestamps, not policy.
- BACKOFF_CONFIG.max capped the blind ladder at 5 min, so a spent
  account was re-probed ~288 times a day forever. Raised to 30 min; the
  ladder still needs ~9 consecutive failures to get there, so transient
  throttles are unaffected.
- 402 fell into the generic 2 min rule even when the body said the
  monthly allowance was gone. Added a `monthly` cooldown class (6h) for
  providers that report a monthly quota without a reset time.

Two executors now report the reset time they already receive:

- antigravity: a 429 from cloudcode-pa carries
  `error.details[].metadata.quotaResetTimeStamp` (plus `quotaResetDelay`
  and `RetryInfo.retryDelay`). Surfaced as `resetsAtMs`, so the model
  lock lasts until the quota returns. Quotas there are per model, so
  only the exhausted model is locked and the other pools stay usable.
- gemini-cli: same API shape — reuses the shared parser and keeps its
  existing `retryAfter` behaviour.
- kiro: splits errors into a human `message` and a machine `reason`, and
  the reason is the only part naming the exhausted allowance
  (`402 MONTHLY_REQUEST_COUNT`). Default parsing dropped it, so the new
  monthly rule could never match. It is now kept in the message.

The Google duration/timestamp parsing lives in one place,
open-sse/utils/googleQuota.js, since both Google-backed executors need
it. Tests use response bodies captured verbatim from live providers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(oauth): background token keep-alive so idle connections stay valid

Access tokens are only ever refreshed on the request path or when
someone opens the usage page. A provider with a short-lived token —
xai/grok-cli issues 6h tokens — therefore expires whenever traffic goes
elsewhere for a few hours, and recovery then depends on the refresh
token still being accepted much later. For providers that rotate or
expire refresh tokens, the account is simply lost, which reads to the
user as "I have to re-authorize every day".

Adds a scheduler in the shape of quotaAutoPing that walks every active
oauth connection and calls the existing
refreshAndUpdateCredentials(conn, false, proxyOptions). That function
already no-ops unless the executor says the token is inside its refresh
window, so an idle install makes zero upstream calls and no per-provider
code is needed — every provider with a refresh path is covered.

Two supporting fixes in refreshAndUpdateCredentials:

- It returned `{refreshed: false}` both when no refresh was due AND when
  the provider rejected the refresh token, so a failed refresh was
  indistinguishable from a healthy no-op. It now also reports
  `refreshFailed: true`, and the keep-alive persists that into
  `lastError` — until now a dead refresh token only produced a
  console.warn, and the dashboard showed the downstream 401 instead.
- `lastRefreshAt` was written only when a provider happened to return
  it, which almost none do. A successful refresh therefore left no
  trace. Now stamped on every successful refresh.

The keep-alive deliberately never writes modelLock_* or isActive:
cooldowns stay owned by the request path. A connection that fails is
backed off for 30 min rather than retried every tick.

Off switch: settings.tokenKeepAliveEnabled = false.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(models): add Model Access page to gate what the endpoint serves

Blocking a model was only reachable from a single provider's page, and there
was no one place to see what the final endpoint actually exposes. On a setup
with many connected providers it is hard to tell which of the models on
/v1/models are intentional.

Add a Model Access page that lists every model of every connected provider,
split into allowed and blocked, with search, an all/allowed/blocked filter, a
per-model toggle, and per-provider bulk actions that operate on the currently
shown set.

This reuses the existing per-provider disabled list that /v1/models already
filters on, so blocking here removes the model from the endpoint rather than
introducing a second, parallel gating mechanism.

Also add a Fetch Models button to the provider page for providers that did not
already have one (OpenAI-compatible providers keep their existing "Import from
/models"), so the listed models can come from the provider's own catalogue via
an active account instead of only the static registry, plus allowed/blocked
count badges.

fix(translator): drop JSON Schema keywords Gemini has no field for

Agent tool schemas routinely carry `uniqueItems` on arrays and the 2020-12
keywords below. The Gemini schema proto has no field for them, so a single
occurrence anywhere in a tool definition fails the whole request with
`400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: Unknown name "uniqueItems" ...: Cannot find field`,
naming a path like
`request.tools[0].function_declarations[83].parameters.properties[0]...`.

A client sending many tools hits this on every call, so the model looks
completely unusable while models on other providers work fine.

Add them to UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINTS so they are stripped like the
neighbouring `minItems`/`maxItems`/`format` constraints already are. Confirmed
against the live API: `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `multipleOf`,
`unevaluatedProperties` and `contentSchema` are all rejected, while `pattern`,
`prefixItems`, `minProperties` and `maxProperties` are accepted and are left
alone.

fix(usage): don't lose cached tokens in the forced-SSE→JSON path

When a provider forces streaming but the client asked for JSON,
handleForcedSSEToJson assembles the response — and cached prompt tokens were lost
on the way out, in two separate ways.

1. The Responses branch built usage from input_tokens alone. On a cache-capable
   upstream input_tokens EXCLUDES cached tokens, so prompt_tokens was
   under-reported: observed 2012 where the real prompt was ~5344 with 5332 served
   from cache. It now folds cache_read + cache_creation into the total and
   surfaces both in prompt_tokens_details. The recorded request detail uses the
   same cache-inclusive total so stored usage and the client response cannot
   disagree.

2. The Chat Completions branch had correct usage — it is the same object written
   to the usage DB — but it did not always reach the client. Reproduced with
   Anthropic reporting cache_read_input_tokens: 11022 while the client received
   no usage field at all. It is now re-attached explicitly before serialisation.

Why it matters: a caller cannot distinguish a 90%-cached request from a cheap one,
so any cost accounting downstream of the proxy is blind. It is worst when 9router
instances are chained, because only the hop that talks to Anthropic natively ever
sees the real numbers.

Verified against a live Claude connection with a fingerprinted payload matched on
both sides of the hop. Also checked, and NOT the cause: the CLAUDE→OPENAI
translator emits prompt_tokens_details correctly (unit-tested with a synthetic
stream carrying cache_read_input_tokens), addBufferToUsage preserves details, and
filterUsageForFormat's OpenAI allowlist includes them.

One nearby trap worth knowing: filterUsageForFormat keys its allowlists by field
NAME, so passing OpenAI-shaped usage with a CLAUDE target returns {} and silently
empties it. Not the cause here, but one mismatched argument away from being.

fix(claude): stop one client's anthropic-beta leaking onto every request

A Claude Code session with the 1M-context beta enabled made unrelated requests
fail with 429 "Usage credits are required for long context requests." — even a
4-token prompt. Reproduced against api.anthropic.com: identical tiny request
returns 200 with beta `oauth-2025-04-20,claude-code-20250219` and 429 the moment
`context-1m-2025-08-07` is added. That beta is pay-as-you-go, so subscription
(OAuth) accounts are not entitled to it, and it is Sonnet-specific — which is
why claude-sonnet-4-6 failed while claude-opus-5 kept working, and why it looked
like a quota problem when quota was fine.

Two faults, both fixed:

1. claudeHeaderCache cached `anthropic-beta` as an "identity" header in a
   process-global singleton, and claudeOverlay applied it to EVERY outbound
   claude request — so one client's entitlement flags rode along on every other
   client's calls. anthropic-beta is request-scoped, not an identity trait; it is
   no longer cached. Outbound flags come from the provider registry's curated
   static list (which includes oauth-2025-04-20 and excludes context-1m).

2. The overlay wrote merged flags BACK into the singleton
   (`cached[lcKey] = ...`), so beta flags accumulated monotonically and survived
   every later request — no rate-limit-lock clearing or account rotation could
   shake them off, only a pod restart. The overlay now treats the cache as
   read-only and builds a local object.

Tests: cache must not retain anthropic-beta; a cached context-1m must never
reach outbound headers; repeated buildHeaders must not mutate the cache; the
static Title-Case Anthropic-Beta must survive without a shadowing lowercase
copy. Verified no regression — header-adjacent suites (golden-url-header,
golden-request, executor-const-guard, force-stream-config) are identical
before/after at 103 passed / 9 pre-existing failures.

fix(headroom): stop an extras install from destroying the CLI

Installing the `ml` extra from the dashboard left headroom undetectable
("not present") on a live instance. Two independent faults:

1. The spec had no version floor. `ml` needs torch, which publishes no wheel
   for musl/Python 3.14, so pip backtracked through 0.4.x/0.3.x looking for a
   release where the extra doesn't exist and picked 0.2.2 — a silent downgrade.
   Its half-finished uninstall removed the `headroom` console script while
   leaving dist-info behind, so `pip list` still said 0.5.4 but `which
   headroom` found nothing. Now floored at the installed version, so pip
   reports the real conflict (ResolutionImpossible) and touches nothing.

2. The image deleted __pycache__ to save space, so bytecode dirs were created
   at runtime owned by whichever uid imported first. A root-owned __pycache__
   in this node-owned venv is what made pip's uninstall die with EACCES
   mid-operation. Pre-compile at build time and chown instead.

Failed installs now surface EXTRA_UNAVAILABLE with a platform explanation
rather than pip's resolver wall-of-text.

Verified on the built image: the previously-destructive
`headroom-ai[proxy,code,ml]` install now fails with the CLI still intact
(binary present, 0.5.4, no downgrade). Note neither extra is installable at
runtime in this image — `ml` has no musl wheel and `code`'s
tree-sitter-language-pack needs a C toolchain the runtime stage lacks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 662ae1a0acff675b82f30f6a15afea9ea902d2ec)

fix: exempt OPTIONS preflight from auth on /v1/* paths (#1381)

Browsers send OPTIONS preflight requests without auth headers by design
(CORS spec). The auth guard in dashboardGuard.js was rejecting these with
401 before any route handler could respond, blocking all cross-origin
browser/WebView clients (browser extensions, Claude for Office, etc.).

Fix: short-circuit OPTIONS on /v1/* paths with a 204 + CORS headers before
the auth check. GET/POST auth is fully preserved.

Also echoes Access-Control-Request-Headers instead of using the wildcard
which some browsers reject during preflight.

Closes #1381
Supersedes #1385 (which patches route handlers that never run because
middleware rejects OPTIONS first)
